title: Théorie de Kumer ? + note Alexandre (bi tenseur…) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: V is a complete noetherian discrete valuation ring with residue field k and fraction field K. The page gives the standard description of the Galois theory of K, the opening of the theme 'Théorie de Kummer'.

(a) Case char(k) = 0 and k algebraically closed. Then char(K) = 0 as well; Grothendieck first wrote car(K) and corrected it to car(k).
- Every finite extension L/K is totally ramified, hence tamely ramified, since the residue extension is trivial and the characteristic is 0. Its Galois closure has Galois group equal to its inertia group, which is cyclic because the wild part is trivial.
- So every finite extension is abelian and cyclic. Since K contains all roots of unity (they lift from k by Hensel's lemma), these extensions are Kummer extensions K(π^{1/n}).
- K*/K*^n ≅ Z/nZ via the valuation. Indeed K* = π^Z × V*, and V* = k* × (1 + m). Here k* is n-divisible because k is algebraically closed, and 1 + m is n-divisible by Hensel's lemma since n is invertible.
- With K̄ an algebraic closure, Kummer theory then gives a canonical isomorphism Gal(K̄/K) ≅ T_∞(k) = lim_n μ_n(k) ≅ Ẑ. This is the Tate module of G_m over k, i.e. Ẑ(1). The canonical map sends σ to the system (σ(π^{1/n})/π^{1/n})_n, which is independent of the choice of uniformizer π. Each μ_n(k) is cyclic of order n.

(b) Case char(k) = p > 0 (k still algebraically closed). The note says completeness of V is not necessary (henselian should suffice). The analogous statement is that the prime-to-p quotient of π_1(K) maps to lim_{(n,p)=1} μ_n(k) = Ẑ'(1). This is an isomorphism: it is the tame quotient of the inertia group (equal here to the whole Galois group, since k is algebraically closed). The wild inertia is a pro-p group, and the full π_1(K) is not determined by this description.

Purpose: this sets up the local Kummer/tame description of inertia as Ẑ'(1). This is the local input for Grothendieck–Murre tame fundamental groups, monodromy around divisors, and the Galois-theoretic / anabelian themes of the 1980s.
errors: The isomorphism K*/K*^n ≅ Z/nZ needs n invertible in k (or char k = 0) and k algebraically closed (n-divisible). This is fine in case (a) but must be restricted to (n,p)=1 in case (b).

For V 'pas nécessairement complet': the statement holds if V is strictly henselian. For an arbitrary non-complete DVR, π_1(K) is much larger (e.g. function fields), and only the inertia group (Galois group of the strict henselization's fraction field) maps onto lim μ_n(k). The note leaves this hypothesis implicit.
In case (b) the arrow is in fact an isomorphism from the maximal prime-to-p quotient, i.e. the tame quotient; the note writes only an arrow. Minor and not an error.

ideas.what: Galois group of the fraction field of a complete DVR with algebraically closed residue field of characteristic 0 is canonically lim μ_n(k) = Ẑ(1); all finite extensions are cyclic Kummer extensions K(π^{1/n})
ideas.modern_name: Structure of tame inertia / local Kummer theory; Ẑ(1) as inertia group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Hasse, Krull, Chevalley); textbook form in Serre, Corps locaux (1962)
ideas.where_published: SGA 1 Exp. XIII; SGA 7 Exp. I; Grothendieck–Murre, LNM 208 (tame fundamental group)

ideas.what: Prime-to-p (tame) quotient of π_1(K) for henselian V with algebraically closed residue field of char p is lim_{(n,p)=1} μ_n(k)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; Serre Corps locaux IV; Grothendieck–Murre 1971

deep.surprise_reason: A textbook recollection of local Kummer theory and tame inertia, standard since Serre's Corps locaux and used throughout SGA 1/SGA 7. It is likely preparatory notes for a course or explanation; nothing new.
